(Today through Thursday)...
Issued at 248 AM EST Fri Nov 13 2026

A strong upper low will pivot across the eastern Great Lakes 
through early Saturday...maintaining scattered light precipitation 
and chilly temperatures today. As the upper trough moves away to the 
east this weekend...dry weather will return with temperatures 
gradually warming next week as broad ridging aloft and at the 
surface expands across the region.

Today through Saturday Night

Scattered light showers continue to drift south across parts of the 
forecast area early this morning. A north-south fetch of heavier 
showers was organizing off of Lake Michigan and extending south 
along the Illinois-Indiana border across the northwest part of the 
state. Brisk northwest winds persisted with 07Z temperatures in the 
upper 30s and lower 40s.

Central Indiana will remain under the influence of the deep upper 
level trough over the eastern part of the country today and at least 
to some degree on Saturday as well. Additional shortwaves will pivot 
around the flank of the upper level trough maintaining plenty of low 
level clouds and periodic light precipitation today. 

As mentioned above...a pronounced northerly fetch off Lake Michigan 
has led to the development of a persistent north-south band of rain 
across northwest Indiana over the last few hours. As the boundary 
layer cools into the predawn hours...rain is expected to mix with or 
changeover to snow within a narrow band that should primarily 
confine itself to immediate downwind areas of Lake and potentially 
western Porter Counties. A mix of light rain and snow will extend 
further south and may be able to briefly make it into the northern 
Wabash Valley largely to the west of KLAF later this morning...aided 
by another shortwave axis dropping through the region. As low level 
temps modify slowly...the predominant precip type should transition 
back largely to rain into the early afternoon. 

Model soundings do show a saturated airmass through about 700mb with 
modest lapse rates through early afternoon...with slightly drier air 
filtering into the boundary layer by late day. Expect a healthy 
stratocu deck to linger across much of the area as a result with the 
potential for sprinkles or flurries for parts of the forecast area 
generally to the east of Interstate 65 through mid afternoon. The 
aforementioned north-south precipitation band will persist in the 
vicinity of the Illinois-Indiana border into this evening before 
decreasing flow within the boundary layer enables it to retreat 
northward. Will maintain at least a small chance for light rain or 
snow showers over the far northwest parts of the forecast area to 
account. 

As a final shortwave swings south of the region during the second 
half of the evening...low level flow will back in tandem with drier 
air gradually advecting into the region overnight. This will result 
in a slow scattering of low clouds from the west as the night 
progresses. Scattered to broken stratocu will redevelop on Saturday 
but should largely remain confined to the northeast half of the 
forecast area in closest proximity to the departing upper low. Low 
clouds will linger across northeast counties Saturday night with 
skies clearing elsewhere as a strong high pressure ridge expands 
into the area from the west. 

Temps...nudged temperatures below the model blend for today as highs 
should range from the low to mid 40s from north to south. Saturday 
will only see marginal improvement as cold air aloft lingers on the 
western flank of the upper trough. Highs Saturday will range from 
the mid 40s northeast to near 50 in the lower Wabash Valley. Lows 
will range from the mid 20s to lower 30s both tonight and Saturday 
night.

Sunday through Late Next Week

The upper low will shift east into the Canadian Maritimes on Sunday 
with an overall transition to broad ridging aloft that will persist 
for much of next week. Scattered to broken stratocu is likely to 
linger across the northeast half of the forecast area on Sunday as 
the upper low slowly moves away. A broad high pressure ridge will 
then pivot into the Ohio Valley with a return to quiet weather and 
mainly clear skies that will last for much of next week. Any 
potential for rain will likely hold off until next weekend at the 
earliest at this point. The onset of warm advection will usher in a 
slow warming trend with seasonable conditions for mid November by 
the middle of next week. Highs will rise steadily through the period 
with lower to mid 60s by late next week.
